# nself add

<!-- BEGIN PROSE:summary -->
> Install a plugin or bundle.
<!-- END PROSE:summary -->

## Synopsis

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED:synopsis -->
<!-- GENERATED BY tools/wikigen — DO NOT HAND EDIT -->
```
nself add <name> [name...] [flags]
```
<!-- END GENERATED:synopsis -->

## Description

<!-- BEGIN PROSE:description -->
Install a plugin or bundle by name.

This is the short form of `nself add`, with bundle awareness: if
the name is a bundle (`nchat`, `nclaw`, `ntv`, `nfamily`, `clawde`, `nsentry`)
the whole bundle is installed, otherwise the name is resolved as a plugin.

Third-party plugins install by URL rather than by name:

  nself add https://example.com/my-plugin.tar.gz

Once installed, the plugin's commands are available directly:

  nself add waf
  nself waf status

Use `nself add waf --plan` to preview generated files, host effects and
container changes before installation, including on production environments.
The registry package and dependencies are verified in temporary staging, then
discarded. The project, installed plugins, database and running stack stay unchanged.
With `--json`, the response has `dry_run: true` and a `plan` member.
Plans currently support individual registry plugins. URL installs, bundles,
builtin toggles, `--version` and non-stable channels are refused before changes.
<!-- END PROSE:description -->
